note:
**`to-write` -> `red` 2026-08-24 19:57Z (vc). THE ROW WAS WRONG AT `to-write`, AND THE INSTRUMENT PASSES -- red is for PARTIAL COVERAGE, held exactly as `AT-00.10` is.** Driven at this revision: `migrate_v2_project.rs` exists, carries `AT-00.6` in its own line-1 doc comment (`AT-10.3 / AT-00.6: ...`), and runs **8 passed, 0 failed** -- read off the `Running` line for that binary, never from a zero-failure workspace total. **The note this replaces said SEVEN. The file gained one and the note did not, which is the smaller half of the same defect.**

**`to-write` WAS NOT A NEUTRAL PARKING SPOT, AND THAT IS THE FINDING RATHER THAN THE SLIP.** `at lint` exempts `to-write` from L2 and L3 -- correctly, since an unwritten test cannot have its citation validated -- so a row parked there is checked by NOTHING. The 2026-08-20 note reasoned carefully and correctly about coverage and then left the row in **the one state where no contract instrument would ever look at it again.** It was found four days later by a COMMIT-GATE staleness check and by no contract instrument, which is the measurement that matters. **A correct analysis parked in an exempt state is indistinguishable from an unexamined row, and it is worse than a wrong one, because the careful reasoning in the note reads as the question having been settled.** Same family as the attestation rule on vc's board: a record that CLOSES a question it did not ANSWER.

**THE PRECEDENT IS MY OWN AND I DID NOT APPLY IT HERE.** `AT-08.5` took this exact transition on 2026-08-19 (ic built it; vc ruled) on the same reasoning, and `AT-00.1` already records *"the harness EXISTS and this row was wrong at `to-write`, which is why it is red rather than merely unwritten."* Both were in front of me. **A ruling made on one row does not propagate to the next by having been made.**

**WHY RED AND NOT GREEN: AC-00.8 IS A FIVE-CLAUSE ROLL-UP AND THIS FILE ASSERTS ONE CLAUSE.**

1. **one visible commit** -- not asserted here; reached by AC-10.3's work.
2. **refuse-lossy residue named** -- asserted in the estate by `AT-10.2` / `AT-10.15`, which cover **AC-10.2**.
3. **`project_id` stamped** -- ASSERTED HERE, by `a_clean_estate_is_stamped_with_a_project_id` and `the_project_id_is_minted_once_and_a_re_run_preserves_it`.
4. **hooks and `settings.json` unchanged** -- asserted in the estate by `AT-10.4`, which covers **AC-10.4**.
5. **documented git-revert rollback** -- documentation (`intent/st/ST0056/migration.md:27`), not a test. **AC-10.6 separately requires it EXERCISED and is unsatisfied; documented and exercised are two criteria and only one is this clause.**

**FOUR OF FIVE CLAUSES ARE NOT ASSERTED BY ANY ROW COVERING THIS CRITERION, AND TWO OF THOSE ARE ASSERTED BY ROWS COVERING OTHER ONES. A criterion is not satisfied because its subject matter is tested somewhere in the estate; it is satisfied when a row that COVERS IT is green.**

**THE COVERAGE RE-CUT IS ROUTED TO hv AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN HERE.** Adding `AC-00.8` to the `covers` of `AT-10.2` and `AT-10.4` is cheap and legitimate -- `covers` is a list and the estate already uses it that way -- and it would satisfy clauses 2 and 4. **It is also the change that conveniently GREENS a criterion, which is this estate's own tell for stopping and routing.** Note the asymmetry that made this fix safe to take alone: **the state correction moves the row in the LOSING direction and needed no ruling; the re-cut moves a number and does.**
